title: fix(deps): bump zod to the fixed line (4.6.1+) workspace-wide, with a regression pin
body:
Fixes #19581

Clause-②: no

Bumps `zod` to the fixed line (4.6.1 or above) workspace-wide, as its own dependency PR, with a regression pin — ruling `5770530634`, letter B.

## The measurement the card asked for first

The ruling asserted 「every workspace range is `^4.4.3`, which already admits the fix」, which would have made this a lockfile-only act. **That premise is false in exactly one place**, and the one place is the only one that actually blocked the bump.

```
git grep -n -E '"zod"[[:space:]]*:' origin/main -- '*package.json'     # 13 files
```

| declarer | before | shape |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `apps/docs` (devDependency, private) | `4.4.3` | **exact pin — does NOT admit 4.6.1** |
| the other 12 (`packages/spec`, `core`, `cli`, `rest`, `runtime`, `objectql`, `metadata`, `metadata-core`, `metadata-protocol`, `mcp`, `driver-turso`, `lint`) | `^4.4.3` | caret — admits 4.6.1 |

The lockfile resolved **all 13 importers to `zod@4.4.3`**, while `zod@4.6.1` was already present (pulled in by the `better-auth` family) — so the ruling's second premise, that the fixed version is already in the store, holds.

What would have made this a different answer: if `apps/docs` had carried a caret like its twelve siblings, no `package.json` would have needed to change and the act really would have been the lockfile alone.

**No `pnpm.overrides` entry is needed, and this was measured rather than assumed.** Every package in the installed tree that declares `zod` — workspace and vendor, hard dependency and peer — carries a range that admits 4.6.1 (`better-auth` family `^4.5.4`, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` `^3.25 || ^4.0`, `fumadocs-mdx` `^4.4.3`, `ai` / `zod-to-json-schema` / `fumadocs-core` / `better-call` as peers). After the bump the lockfile holds **one** zod copy:

```
packages ADDED:   []
packages REMOVED: ["zod@4.4.3"]
```

Nothing else moved: the only `+` lines in the lockfile diff are `version: 4.6.1` / `specifier: ^4.6.1` / `specifier: 4.6.1`, and the removals are `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and `zod-to-json-schema` collapsing from two peer-bracketed copies to one.

Each declaration keeps its **shape** — caret stays caret, `apps/docs`'s exact pin stays exact. Whether that app should carry an exact pin at all is a separate question this PR does not answer. The lockfile was refreshed by `pnpm install`, never hand-edited.

### Why the declared floor moves and not only the lockfile

A lockfile protects this repo's CI. It does not protect anyone who installs `@objectstack/spec`: with `^4.4.3` still declared, a fresh downstream install can resolve 4.4.3 and crash on a refusal **this platform emits**. The floor is the part consumers get.

## The defect, re-measured first-hand

The card said its premise arrived second-hand and asked whoever took it to re-read the vendor source. Done — both versions, from the store, on the three path shapes:

| | zod 4.4.3 | zod 4.6.1 |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `['assignments','__proto__']` (terminal) | `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'push')` | renders |
| `['config','toString']` (terminal) | same `TypeError` | renders |
| `['__proto__','polluted']` (non-terminal) | **returns**, message **missing**, `Object.prototype` **polluted** | renders, no pollution |

All three formatters walked a path by reading `curr[el]` and testing it for truthiness before creating a node, so an element naming an `Object.prototype` member was answered by the prototype. 4.6.1 adds a `node()` helper guarding the read with `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call` and creating a `__proto__` node through `defineProperty`.

**A third formatter the card did not name is affected:** `flattenError` (`error.flatten()`) throws on `__proto__`, `toString` **and** `constructor` even at a single-element path. Same vendor bug, same fix, so it is pinned here rather than filed separately.

## The regression pin, proven to discriminate

`packages/spec/src/shared/zod-error-formatter-proto-path.pin.test.ts` — run byte-identical against both versions, in two real worktrees (this branch, and one at the merge base where the lockfile still pins 4.4.3):

| tree | zod | result |
|:---|:---|:---|
| merge base `eff0a96223` | 4.4.3 | **6 failed, 1 passed** |
| this branch | 4.6.1 | **7 passed** |

The one test that passes on 4.4.3 is the **positive control** ("an ORDINARY path renders the same way"), which is there precisely so the six failures cannot be read as a broken test. Both modes are pinned separately, because a fix that stopped the pollution while still dropping the message would be no fix.

Every lookup goes through an `ownValue` helper (`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`), never a bare `node.__proto__` or `node.toString` — a bare read is answered by the prototype, which is the very confusion the defect is made of. The prototype-pollution canary is a **snapshot** of `Object.prototype`'s own keys rather than a guessed roster: the defect also installs the walker's own container key (`properties`) there, and a fixed roster missed it.

## What moved that was not asked for, and why it is a correction

`gen:docs` regenerated four reference pages: `ViewFilterRule.operator` now renders as **required** where it rendered optional.

That is the docs catching up with the runtime, not a narrowing. `operator` carries no `.optional()`. It is declared through `z.preprocess(normalizeFilterOperator, z.enum(...))`, and a `z.preprocess`'s inner transform hardcodes `_zod.optin = "optional"` regardless of what it wraps — the same vendor quirk `refuseProtoOwnKey` already corrects by hand. Measured on one object with a preprocessed required key:

| | `toJSONSchema(io: 'input').required` |
|:---|:---|
| zod 4.4.3 | `["field"]` |
| zod 4.6.1 | `["operator","field"]` |

4.6.1 stops the requiredness computation from believing that flag; the flag itself is unchanged in both, so the existing `optin`/`optout` correction stays load-bearing and unaffected. The tracked JSON Schemas do not move — `check:authorable-surface` is green.

`content/docs/references/` is auto-generated and may not be hand-edited, so regenerating it is the prescribed step, not scope creep.

## Blast radius inside this repo: zero call sites

Radius: tracked `*.ts` under `packages/`, `apps/`, `examples/`. Zero call sites of `treeifyError` / `formatError` / `flattenError` / `.format()` / `.flatten()` — the only non-pin hit is a comment. Positive control on the same command and radius: `safeParse` fires in **627** files. Known target outside the radius (the formatter definition, in `node_modules`): 0, as expected.

So the crash was never live in this repo's own code. It was live for **consumers** formatting a refusal this platform emits — which is the argument for moving the declared floor.

## Scope widened under ruling `5774631464` — declared, not drifted

Decision batch #212 item 1, letter **A**. The maintainer's words, verbatim and untranslated:

> 「19674 反正要升级,建议一步该到位」

⇒ this PR carries **both halves**: the workspace-wide zod bump with its regression pin, **and** the repair of the view-authoring diagnosis, so a retired value is refused by a message that NAMES it rather than by the 「wrap your content in a container」 prescription.

**File surface beyond the dispatched manifests and the lockfile**, declared as a scope widening under that ruling:

- `packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts` — the repair
- `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` — the three closed shapes that do not come through `strictObject`
- `packages/spec/src/shared/zod-error-formatter-proto-path.pin.test.ts` — the regression pin the ruling asks for (a NEW file)
- `.changeset/19581-zod-formatter-proto-path-bump.md` — extended
- `apps/docs/package.json` — the exact pin moved to the shared range (ruling item 4's stated intent; its premise was stale in both halves, and no recorded reason for the exact *shape* was found)

Changeset level unchanged: **patch** on `@objectstack/spec`.

## The mechanism — it was none of the three candidates the ruling named

zod **4.5.0** adds `continue: true` to the `unrecognized_keys` issue (`v4/core/schemas.js`, both the shape-phase push and `handleCatchall`; absent on 4.4.3). Two consequences:

1. `runChecks` reads `util.aborted(payload)` **once on entry**, so a continuable unknown-key issue lets the same object's `.refine()` / `.superRefine()` run and add a second, contradictory complaint.
2. `util.aborted(result)` is now **false** for a member whose only complaint is an unknown key ⇒ `handleUnionResults`' single-non-aborted **short-circuit** fires and returns that member's issues **unwrapped** ⇒ the union never raises `invalid_union` ⇒ `focusClaimedBranch`, which only fires on `invalid_union`, never runs.

⭐ The discriminating control: `handleUnionResults` is **byte-identical** on 4.4.3 / 4.5.0 / 4.6.1, so it is not what moved. ⇒ the variable was never inside the view members; it is **generic**.

⚠️ This also falsifies an earlier round's refutation: 「plain `z.union` reports `invalid_union` identically on both lines」 was **vacuous for this mechanism** — a 2-member union whose members both abort never reaches the short-circuit, so that control could not have shown it whatever the truth was.

**The repair**: `closedObject` re-declares a closed shape through a `z.core.$constructor` that marks its unknown-key issue non-continuable **inside `_zod.parse`**, i.e. before `runChecks` reads the payload. A constructor rather than an instance patch because `util.clone()` rebuilds through `_zod.constr`, so `.strict()`, `.extend()`, `.refine()` and `.omit()` carry it forward.

**Before / after**, same body through the same door — without the repair a retired `type: 'page'` reads 「Unrecognized key(s) on this view container… Wrap it: `defineView({ list: … })`」 and the string `page` appears nowhere; with it, code `invalid_union` and 「`config.type: 'page'` was removed from the list-view `type` enum in @objectstack/spec 17.5.0 (ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove)…」.

**Result: 78 failing assertions across 17 files → 4 across 1**, and ⛔ **no existing test was edited** — the only `.test.ts` in the diff is the added regression pin.

⚠️ The vendor reading above is the delivering round's; the seat could not re-derive it (no `node_modules` in a shared checkout, and it will not install into one). It is handed to the at-tier contract review.

## ⛔ Why this is not armed yet

7 assertions remain red — 4 in `packages/spec/src/shared/error-map.test.ts`, 3 in `packages/cli/test/format-zod-union.test.ts`. **One cause**: both pin a formatter expanding an `invalid_union` using a fixture built from raw zod primitives **declared in the test file**, and under the new floor that fixture produces no `invalid_union` at all. ⛔ No production change in either package can reach them. The contract itself is not unpinned — `union-author-message-pins.test.ts` exercises the same expansion through real doors and is green.

⇒ that is a decision, not a defect to patch here: **card #19730**. This card is `pm:blocked` behind it.

## Verified

Run locally, foreground, exit codes captured before any pipe:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build && check:generated` — **15 of 15 artifacts up to date**, exit 0.
- the regression pin, both legs, as tabled above.
- `tsc --noEmit -p packages/spec/tsconfig.test.json` — 0 errors in the new file.

**Not run locally, and named rather than implied:** the workspace-wide `pnpm test` / `pnpm typecheck`, the repo-wide `pnpm lint`, and the other gate families a dependency bump schedules. A workspace-wide bump's blast radius is the whole workspace and that belongs to CI, which runs it on this PR. If a suite fails on this bump, that is a finding about the bump and belongs in a comment here — not a licence to edit the failing tests.

## Acceptance notes

- `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json` records `"measured": { "zod": "4.4.3" }` as provenance. Nothing gates that field and the ledger's counts did not move, so it is left alone rather than re-stamped without a re-measure. Successor: whoever next changes refinement projection.
- `@objectstack/lint` moves only a devDependency range, so nothing it publishes changes for a consumer and it takes no release in the changeset.
- The declared collision with PR #19642 over the root `package.json` **did not materialise**: no override was needed, and this repo's `overrides` live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` regardless — pnpm v10 silently ignores a `pnpm.overrides` block in `package.json`, as that file's own header states.
